name: Secure a WP-CLI purge command against SQL injection
query: This plugin has a WP-CLI command `wp my-plugin purge` that deletes rows older than a given number of days from a custom logs table. It runs fine locally and we want to schedule it in CI, so give it a security once-over and fix anything risky.
expected_behavior: Locate the command registered with WP_CLI::add_command() and its method that reads $args and runs the DELETE query
Identify the flaw: the CLI argument is interpolated directly into the $wpdb->query() SQL string instead of using $wpdb->prepare()
Sanitize the positional argument to its expected type with absint(), using isset() to apply a safe default when the argument is missing
Rewrite the query through $wpdb->prepare() with a %d placeholder so no $args value is ever interpolated into SQL
Fail fast with WP_CLI::error() when the sanitized value is invalid, before any query runs
Report the result with WP_CLI::success() (or WP_CLI::log()/WP_CLI::error()) instead of echo
success_criteria: No CLI argument is interpolated into SQL; the dynamic DELETE query goes through $wpdb->prepare() with a %d placeholder
The positional argument is sanitized with absint() and an isset() default, matching the expected integer type
Invalid input exits via WP_CLI::error() before any database query executes
The injection is resolved: arbitrary SQL appended to the CLI argument can no longer execute
